articles.title: El capitán de Chile advierte: "Jugar contra España y como locales es una oportunidad que hay que aprovechar"
articles.standfirst: Nicolás Massú destaca la versatilidad del equipo español antes de la eliminatoria de clasificación previa a la fase final que se disputa esta semana en Santiago
articles.summary: Nicolás Massú destaca la versatilidad del equipo español antes de la eliminatoria de clasificación previa a la fase final que se disputa esta semana en Santiago
articles.body: El capitán del equipo de Chile de Copa Davis, Nicolás Massú, que el próximo fin de semana se va a enfrentar a España en Santiago, en la eliminatoria de clasificación previa a la fase final, se mostró entusiasmado por el desafío que supone para su selección jugar ante "uno de los mejores del mundo en una oportunidad que hay que aprovechar". Chile no pierde una eliminatoria como local en esta competición desde hace quince años, desde que cayó en septiembre el 2011 ante Italia. Desde que Massú es el capitán del equipo, nunca ha perdido una serie como anfitrión. Este fin de semana, en el Court Central Anita Lizana de Santiago, afronta otro reto. "Mi prioridad era poner a Chile entre los mejores del mundo. Tener una oportunidad de jugar contra España, en casa, hay que aprovecharla. Que vengan países de potencia mundial no siempre pasa. Puede tocarte varios años como visitante y hay que aprovechar jugar como local. Vamos a asumir esta serie con convicción. Uno vive para enfrentarse a los mejores del mundo. Esta generación puede dar mucho más al tenis chileno", dijo Massú. El capitán de Chile destaca la variedad del conjunto español a pesar de no contar con Carlos Alcaraz ni Alejandro Davidovich y su facilidad para adaptarse a distintas superficies. "Todos hablan de Rafael Jódar y nos vamos a enfrentar a él. Es una fecha impresionantemente especial para Chile el 18 de septiembre. Todo se junta. Me contaron que las entradas se vendieron en cuatro horas. Hay que trabajar para que el día de mañana podamos seguir creciendo", insistió Massú. "Los jugadores españoles se adaptan a todas las superficies. Se adaptan muy rápido. Tres son de Madrid, Dani Mérida, Martín Landaluce y Rafa Jódar y saben jugar en esta superficie. Más que preocuparse de la situación y las circunstancias y si puede llover o no, hay que centrarse en nuestro equipo", añadió el responsable del equipo chileno, que subraya lo especial de la fecha en la que se inicia el duelo ante el cuadro de David Ferrer. "Es una fecha especial además, el 18 de septiembre, las Fiestas Patrias (conmemoración la conformación de la Primera junta Nacional de Gobierno en 1810). Es una serie que tiene todo para ser espectacular. Ante uno de los mejores del mundo, en casa", indicó Nicolás Massú, que afronta otra serie relevante en su carrera. "Todas las Copas Davis son importantes. Y cada serie se toma con mucha seriedad. Desde que soy capitán nunca se ha perdido como local pero España es una potencia mundial. Es finalista. Tiene un equipo muy bueno y si jugamos con ello es porque nos hemos mantenido en el tiempo, en el Grupo Mundial. Medirse y competir con España es que estamos arriba, entre los dieciséis mejores del mundo", recordó. Massú cuenta con Alejandro Tabilo, Cristian Garin, Tomás Barrios y Matías Soto como selección. No podrá contar con Nicolas Jarry, que acaba de salir de una lesión. "Nos hubiera gustado que también Nico Jarry estuviera en el equipo y uno a veces no puede contar con todos los jugadores. Garín, que llegó también con limitaciones físicas, está entrenando bien y eso me da tranquilidad. Para cuando tome la decisión esté apto para poder jugar. El jueves sabrán quiénes son los elegidos para jugar", añadió. "Siempre lo importante es ocuparme de nosotros primero. Evaluar a España, por ránking es un equipo muy bueno. Alejandro Davidovich y Carlos Alcaraz no están. A nosotros también nos faltan jugadores pero tienen jugadores muy potentes, jóvenes. Han tenido grandes resultados en arcilla y cemento. Vamos a ver quienes son los de individuales. La localía es importante para nosotros. Jugamos en cancha de arcilla con nuestras condiciones. Tenemos confianza pero qué mejor que enfrentarse a equipos de los mejores del mundo porque eso quiere decir que estamos ahí", insistió Massú. Nicolás Massú compatibiliza su trabajo en el circuito, a lo largo de la temporada, con el argentino Francisco Cerúndolo, con el de capitán de Copa Davis. "Llevo tantos años en el circuito y ahora estoy centrado en la Copa Davis. La emoción de representar a Chile en el estadio Nacional. Queremos seguir creciendo y compitiendo. Ahora estoy con Francisco Cerúndolo en el circuito y cuando acabe la Davis volveré al tour con él. Sigo motivado". "La responsabilidad de un capitán es tomar decisiones. Cuando se trata de lesiones tengo un equipo médico que me aconseja y también el médico de cada jugador. siento su apoyo y me pueden aconsejar. Tengo experiencia, jugué esta competición y también soy capitán desde hace tiempo. Sé lo que están haciendo los jugadores españoles y a quién nos vamos a enfrentar. Todo es parte del trabajo. La Copa Davis para mi es mi vida. Representar a Chile es una prioridad", dijo Massú sobre los lesionados, como Jarry que a pesar de la lesión está con el grupo chileno y es una aportación en los entrenamientos. Sufre una dolencia en el codo derecho y lleva sin competir desde abril. "Nico lleva un tiempo sin competir. está en recuperación y empezó a jugar en cancha la semana pasada. Quería que estuviera con nosotros entrenando. Está con nosotros y es importante para el grupo, lleva tiempo en la Copa Davis. Me tiene contento. Somos ocho jugadores aquí y es lo que uno quiere. Hay jugadores con más tiempo y con menos tiempo y espero que se recupere que pueda jugar torneos y que tenga motivación por estar con nosotros", concluyó Massú.

articles.title: German tennis star takes a jab at Trinity Rodman & losers try to cancel Ella Langley over old hunting photos
articles.summary: Ella Langley faces online backlash over old deer hunting photos, while Trinity Rodman rushes to the US Open and Aryna Sabalenka's fashion sparks debate.
articles.body: 'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com. Wow, the Dolphins are really bad. We're not talking the usual levels of Miami Dolphins bad. We're talking about 1–15 bad, à la 2007. Except it'll be 1-16 now. If they're lucky to squeak out that one W at all. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE But you know what? I'm at peace with it. As a lifelong Dolphins fan, I'm accustomed to sadness, disappointment and misery. That's because every year when Week 1 rolls around — despite knowing better — I delude myself into thinking "this season will be better!" I'm like Amy Klobuchar wearing the same dumb shirt and the same goofy grin. This year, I have no such delusions. Every week, I fully understand the team will s---- itself worse than that HYROX chick. Only this time, instead of a quarterback who gets concussed every other week, we have one who runs fast and wears rhinestone cleats. Ah, the serenity of low expectations. I'm as carefree as Bo Nix. So with that, let's get to our Tuesday Nightcaps — featuring Trinity Rodman, Ella Langley and Aryna Sabalenka. And there will be nothing about Sydney Sweeney, Holly Rowe or Arch Manning. Because I'm tired of hearing about all of them. Let's roll. The mob tries to cancel Ella Langley over hunting photos Some people really don't like Ella Langley. I've heard a multitude of reasons for this: She cut a song with Morgan Wallen. She followed Charlie Kirk on TikTok. She got some lip filler. She's allegedly MAGA. The real reason is probably because "Choosin' Texas" has spent a bazillion weeks at No. 1, and a good chunk of our population just likes to hate on people who are successful. But now, the miserable souls of the interweb have found a new reason to smear the good name of Ella Langley — she's a hunter! Some folks with too much time on their hands dug up some old photos of Ella showing off bucks she harvested in her home state of Alabama. I love how that second post said she'd been "caught" hunting animals. As if Ella didn't pose for that photo and post it on her own social media account. Damn, you really busted her! Let's see what the comments are saying. Very sane people over there on the Twitter machine. As the founding mother of OutKick OutDoors, I'm obviously pro (legal and humane) hunting and fishing. And I won't bore you with all the reasons why hunting — particularly whitetail deer hunting — is crucial for conservation, preventing the spread of disease, and funding for the protection of wildlife and their habitats. I encourage you to do your own research if you're interested in learning more. JORDAN DAVIS FACES FAN BACKLASH OVER HAWAII AXIS DEER HUNT DESPITE STRONG CONSERVATION BACKING I also have no problem with people who choose not to hunt or choose not to eat meat. That's absolutely your prerogative. But I guarantee at least 99% of the people screeching at Ella right now have no problem stopping by the Taco Bell drive-thru or picking up a pack of chicken at the grocery store. But harvesting your own fresh venison apparently makes you evil. Spare me the outrage, losers. Alexander Zverev throws shade at Trinity Rodman Trinity Rodman is a world-class soccer player for the USWNT. But she's also a tennis WAG. So while her boyfriend, Ben Shelton, competed in the US Open the past couple of weeks, Trinity was in the stands supporting him. Unfortunately for Trinity (and America), Shelton lost to Germany's Alexander Zverev in the men's final. That's after she played a soccer game in Washington, D.C. on the same day and then rushed 200 miles to NYC to catch the end of the match. When he won, Zverev gave Trinity a shoutout. "Trinity, I thought you have a game today," Zverev joked. "Well done to you as well. You’re the lucky charm ... not today, but usually." The crowd laughed. Trinity laughed. Ben laughed. And then Iman Shumpert wanted to see Ben defend his lady's honor. "I ain't gonna lie, Ben, get up in there, you gotta say something. I ain't gonna lie, he just shot..." Shumpert said. "You need a rematch. Yeah, you gotta treat it like boxing. Hey, Ben, go get your get back, buddy." Zverev might have stolen the Grand Slam title. But I don't think she's stealing Shelton's girl. She seems pretty into him. Let's open the mailbag. 📩 Email: amber.harding@outkick.com (Send your thoughts, stories, tips, rants and photos of your dog.) 🐦 Twitter/X: @TheAmberHarding 📸 Instagram: @amberharding No one cares about women's basketball ...at least according to Keith H. Keith writes: No one watches Women’s basketball and no one cares about whatever "tournament" is going on. The only things more boring are Women’s hockey, Women’s soccer, and watching paint dry. Amber: Folks, Keith cares so little about women's basketball that he clicked on a story about the USA women's basketball team's semifinal game against Spain. Then, he found the writer (me) and typed out an email about how much he doesn't care. On a Saturday night. While college football was on. Going to such lengths suggests to me that Keith actually cares a lot about women's basketball. Listen, folks, the reason we cover so much WNBA is because our women's basketball coverage consistently performs spectacularly well in metrics like page views, search and engagement. If it didn't, we wouldn't spend so much time and energy writing about it. All of our show hosts wouldn't be talking about it. And we certainly wouldn't send a reporter all the way to Europe to cover it. We give the people what they want. And even the "hate reads" count as page views, baby. More love for Upstate New York A couple of weeks ago, I wrote about making my first trip to the St. Lawrence River in Upstate New York. But it certainly won't be my last. Brian S. writes: It’s not a very manly phrase, I realize, but I was tickled pink reading your reaction to the St. Lawrence River. I was born - 1969 - and raised in Upstate New York. The River and 1,000 Islands have been a destination for my family since the 40’s. We grew up trailer camping in the state parks there, before renting cottages once we outgrew the camper, and eventually my folks purchased a summer home in Cape Vincent, a short drive from Clayton, where you were. My now adult children looked forward to every summer stay, even though the drive from New Jersey is about 5-1/2 hours. Whenever I bring friends to the area for the first time, they all have the same reaction as you had. We may have even crossed paths last weekend, as my wife and I were there visiting for a few days, and we even checked out the Bassmasters tourney. I’m glad you were able to experience the beauty of the region, and hope you’re able to visit again in the future. Amber: Every summer, my husband and I like to retreat to Lake Superior, and the St. Lawrence area area reminded me a lot of the Northwoods. There's just something so serene about the small towns around the Great Lakes. Everything's just slower there — in the best way possible. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Who cares what Aryna Sabalenka is wearing? Lucia writes: May I ask why the uproar over Sabalenka’s choice of tennis attire, but I hear nothing about Osaka’s abysmal fashion choices. First, let’s ask why she needs an entrance ‘outfit’? They definitely say ‘look at me’, but I don’t see them as making much of a statement about her tennis skills. Secondly, Osaka’s court wear yesterday could have very easily been made out of the Hefty Bags you referenced in your article. With that said, I’m not a fan of Sabalenka’s attire either. Nike should be embarrassed they put their ‘swoosh’ on the fishnet. While she may have a contractual obligation, she and her management should have put their respective foot down. Lastly, I don’t understand why the urge to make a ‘fashion’ statement has become a thing. Used to be the serve, the smash, the volley said it all. Amber: To be fair, I have seen plenty of people poke fun at Osaka's wild get-ups. I think the entrance outfit and the non-traditional kits are just part of tennis culture right now. It's like NFL and NBA players playing dress-up just to walk from their cars into the stadium on game day. Sabalenka's mesh kit wasn't my favorite, either. But it got us talking. And that was probably Nike's goal. One more thing: 'South Park' is back tomorrow My fellow "South Park" super fans will likely agree that last season was the worst one yet. No, not because they made fun of Trump. They made fun of Trump for five whole seasons when they had an orange-faced Mr. Garrison acting as President of the United States. The difference is that those seasons were original, funny and clever. This past season was none of those things. It was just Trump having a "butt baby" with Satan and the same "small d—" joke over and over and over. We get it. Even my liberal friends were like, "Can we please go back to the actual characters of 'South Park?'" But, naturally, Hollywood loved it. So Trey Parker and Matt Stone were awarded their first Emmy. Well, "South Park" is back tomorrow. Except they're calling it "South America" to make fun of Trump's renaming of the Gulf of Mexico and Lake Ontario. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER And you know what? Cool. That's the kind of satire they should be doing. And judging by the trailer, it's actually going to be about the boys this time. So, fingers crossed, this season won't just be another giant turd sandwich. You sold out and got your Emmy, Matt and Trey. Now please go back to being funny.

articles.title: Aryna Sabalenka’s nightmare deepens as Elena Rybakina takes both US Open title and No. 1 ranking within 72 hours
articles.summary: International Sports News: Aryna Sabalenka’s US Open campaign ended with more than a painful final defeat. In just three days, the Belarusian lost the world No. 1 ranking and th.
articles.body: Aryna Sabalenka’s US Open campaign ended with more than a painful final defeat. In just three days, the Belarusian lost the world No. 1 ranking and then watched her bid for a third straight US Open title disappear against Elena Rybakina. The collapse marked a rare low point in Sabalenka’s recent Grand Slam run, but her response afterward showed that she is already thinking about getting back to the top.Aryna Sabalenka loses world No. 1 ranking to Elena RybakinaThe warning signs had been building before Sabalenka even reached the US Open final.Rybakina had entered the tournament with a genuine chance to overtake Sabalenka at No. 1. Her rise had gained momentum after she defeated Sabalenka in the WTA Finals Riyadh championship match at the end of 2025. She then produced another dramatic win over the Belarusian at the Australian Open, recovering from a 3-0 deficit in the deciding set.Sabalenka knew the ranking battle was becoming difficult to ignore. Yet she tried to keep her attention on the court.“I completely separate myself from that, because it’s just guessing. It’s like if, if, if, if. I’m just trying to bring my best tennis every time I’m competing out there and basically fight for it,” she said after reaching the quarter-finals.Rybakina ultimately made the ranking change unavoidable. She defeated Qinwen Zheng to reach the US Open semi-finals, officially ending Sabalenka’s 99-week run at No. 1.Sabalenka responded with a short but striking message.“I don’t care!”Her point was clear. A Grand Slam trophy mattered more to her than holding the top ranking.Unfortunately for Sabalenka, she would lose both.Elena Rybakina defeats Sabalenka in US Open finalRybakina entered the final after beating Coco Gauff in the semi-finals, while Sabalenka arrived as the defending champion and favourite. She also carried an impressive record at Arthur Ashe Stadium, having not lost there in two years.The stakes were enormous. A victory would have made Sabalenka only the third woman in tennis history to win the US Open three consecutive times.Rybakina had other plans.The Kazakh player took the opening set 6-4, using her powerful groundstrokes to overcome a difficult start on serve. Sabalenka fought back in the second, breaking late to take it 7-5 and force a deciding set.That comeback proved temporary.Rybakina regained control in the third set, breaking for a 2-1 advantage before adding another break at 5-2. She finished the match with her 12th ace, completing a 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 victory in two hours and 21 minutes.The result gave Rybakina her first US Open title and strengthened her claim as the leading force in women's tennis. When the WTA publishes its updated rankings, she will become the 30th woman in the Open Era to reach No. 1.For Sabalenka, the defeat ended a remarkable run. She will finish 2026 without a Grand Slam title for the first time since 2022.Still, she did not leave New York sounding defeated."I don't even know how many weeks I was able to be there, but it was amazing. Let's see if Elena can beat me in that. If she continues playing like that, I'm in trouble"Her words carried a warning as much as a compliment. Sabalenka may have lost her crown, but she already has her eyes on taking it back.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: Juan Carlos Ferrero confirma en Movistar Plus Deportes que volverá al circuito ATP la temporada que viene
articles.body: En diciembre de 2025 un noticia conmocionó al mundo del tenis. Carlos Alcaraz y Juan Carlos Ferrero anunciaron el final de su relación profesional. El entonces número uno mundial y su entrenador habían permanecido juntos durante toda la carrera profesional del murciano. "Es muy difícil para mí escribir este post… Tras más de siete años juntos, Juanki y yo hemos decidido poner fin a nuestra etapa juntos como entrenador y jugador", escribía Carlitos en su cuenta de Instagram. Por su parte Ferrero reconoció que "hoy es un día difícil. Uno en el que cuesta encontrar las palabras. Despedirse nunca es fácil, y menos cuando detrás hay tantas experiencias compartidas. Hemos trabajado duro, crecido juntos, y compartiendo vivencias inolvidables. Quiero dar las gracias por el tiempo, la confianza, el aprendizaje y, sobre todo, por las personas que me han rodeado durante todo este viaje". Juan Carlos Ferrero confesó, sobre su ruptura con Alcaraz, que "se me partió el corazón, pero me estoy recuperando". Nueve meses después Juan Carlos Ferrero ha confirmado a Movistar Plus Deportes, durante el partido de fútbol que el Real Madrid ganó 2-3 al Elche, que volverá al circuito ATP la temporada que viene. "¿Qué estoy haciendo? Este año tranquilo, con la familia y dedicándome a los niños que me juegan al fútbol en vez de el tenis. articles.summary: "Estoy descubriendo que soy una persona valiente y sigo con los pies en el suelo, siendo la misma persona humilde que era hace dos años"
articles.body: El tenista español Rafael Jódar señaló en Santiago, donde la selección nacional se encuentra para disputar con Chile la segunda ronda eliminatoria de la Copa Davis, que está descubriendo que es una persona valiente. En declaraciones distribuidas por la Real Federación Española de Tenis (RFET), Jódar, decimocuarto del mundo, dijo: "Es verdad que está yendo todo muy rápido, pero al final lo estoy disfrutando. Sigo con los pies en el suelo, siendo la misma persona humilde que era hace dos años, lo cual creo que me está ayudando mucho y eso es gracias a todas las personas que realmente me aprecian y quieren lo mejor para mí". "Veo que puedo competir contra la mayoría de los jugadores en el circuito en mi primer año, lo cual significa que estoy haciendo las cosas muy bien y que, poco a poco, voy entrando en ritmo de competición contra rivales muy diferentes y que tienen un dibujo muy diferente", explica. El madrileño argumentó: "Si quieres estar entre los mejores jugadores del mundo durante muchos años, tienes que cuidar cada detalle al milímetro y hacer todas las cosas muy bien. Saber que va a haber momentos donde las cosas no van a ir como tú quieres, pero aceptar esos momentos, superarlos y tener una mentalidad positiva de siempre ir mejorando poco a poco." En esta línea, el top-15 de la clasificación mundial de la ATP reconoce que: "Si quiero seguir consiguiendo buenos resultados voy a tener que mejorar mucho mi nivel de tenis, voy a tener que aprender mucho a lidiar con jugar muchos torneos en un año, con jugar con diferentes rivales en cada semana o incluso en cada torneo." "El camino -dijo- es disfrutar del proceso, ir mejorando poco a poco. Es mi primer año en el circuito, sé que quedan muchas cosas por mejorar y que todo lo que me pase este año va a ser nuevo para mí van a ser nuevas experiencias". Jódar, que el 17 de este mes cumplirá 20 años, aclaró que nació en Madrid y no en Leganés como muchos piensan: "Jugaba en el Club de Tenis Chamartín desde los seis años. Me he criado en Madrid y he pasado todos los años de mi infancia allí". Confesó: "Estoy descubriendo que soy una persona valiente", y añade que: "tener que lidiar con todo lo que hay alrededor de los torneos es difícil para una persona tan joven, y considero estoy llevando muy bien todo ese tipo de cosas". Rafa también se refirió a la figura de su padre, Rafael, que habitualmente permanece solo en el box de los torneos del circuito. "Es una cosa inusual en el circuito, ya que todos los jugadores o la mayoría de los jugadores tienen a muchas personas en el box. Es el primer año y estamos intentando aprender de cada error que cometemos y de lo que va bien. Este año está funcionando. Nos llevamos muy bien, tenemos una relación muy buena desde que yo era muy pequeño y él siempre me ha ayudado mucho y siempre quiere lo mejor para mí", explicó.

articles.body: La Rafa Nadal Academy iniciará las celebraciones de su décimo aniversario el próximo sábado 3 de octubre con una tarde muy especial de tenis. A partir de las 17:00, Rafa Nadal participará en una serie de partidos de exhibición junto a grandes nombres de este deporte. El ganador de 22 Grand Slam compartirá pista con algunos de los rivales y amigos que le acompañaron a lo largo de su carrera. Será una cita especialmente emotiva ya que Rafa volverá a jugar ante el público por primera vez desde su retirada del tenis profesional, en noviembre de 2024, durante las Finales de la Copa Davis disputadas en Málaga. El 'Rafa Nadal Academy Slam', que se podrá seguir en directo en Movistar Plus, dará el pistoletazo de salida a las celebraciones del décimo aniversario de la Rafa Nadal Academy, una ocasión para poner en valor la evolución de un proyecto nacido en Manacor en 2016 y construido sobre la metodología, la experiencia y los valores que han marcado la trayectoria del manacorí. Desde sus inicios, la Academia ha trabajado para que jóvenes de todo el mundo puedan compaginar su desarrollo deportivo con sus estudios y su formación personal. Una filosofía que entiende el éxito más allá de las pistas y que sitúa el esfuerzo, el respeto y la superación en el centro del aprendizaje. Ese trabajo también se ha traducido en importantes resultados deportivos: sus jugadores han conquistado 14 títulos de Grand Slam júnior (siete individuales y siete de dobles) y cinco han alcanzado el número uno del mundo júnior. Hace apenas tres semanas, siete jugadores de la Academia figuraban simultáneamente en el Top 100 de los rankings ATP y WTA. Entre ellos destaca Alex Eala, una de las grandes figuras emergentes del tenis, cuya trayectoria está generando un notable impacto internacional Durante esta década, ese ADN ha traspasado también las fronteras de Mallorca. La expansión internacional ha sido una de las principales líneas de crecimiento del proyecto, que actualmente cuenta con ocho centros en todo el mundo: Manacor, Costa Mujeres, Grecia, Kuwait, Hong Kong, Marbella, Egipto y Punta Cana.

articles.title: Alex Eala firm on Asian Games participation despite threat of WTA fine
articles.summary: National lawmakers propose paying her fine should WTA impose it on her for skipping the concurrent mandatory China Open.
articles.body:
Filipino tennis star Alex Eala is firm on representing her country at the Asian Games regardless of the Women’s Tennis Association’s (WTA) decision to grant an exemption from the mandatory China Open, the Philippine Tennis Association (PHILTA) has said after filing a request on her behalf.

“We have formally requested an exemption and we respect the WTA’s process. At the same time, Alex has made her decision to represent the Philippines at the Asian Games, and we fully support her,” PHILTA secretary-general John Rey Tiangco told the media on Tuesday.

The world number 18, who has become a fan favourite with wins over some of the biggest names on the circuit, including Iga Swiatek and Coco Gauff, is the highest-ranked player in the women’s singles draw at the Asian Games, which begin on September 19 and conclude on October 4.

However, the Aichi-Nagoya Games schedule overlaps with the mandatory WTA 1000 tournament China Open, which starts in Beijing on September 30.

Skipping a mandatory WTA 1000 competition without an official exemption results in a ranking penalty and may attract fines.

Earlier this week, Indonesian Janice Tjen withdrew from the Asian Games as she was unable to secure an exemption from participating in the China Open.

However, Eala will compete at the Asian Games regardless of the WTA’s decision, Philippine Olympic Committee president Abraham Tolentino said in a statement.

“The WTA has its rules and breaking the rules has penalties. But Alex will be in Nagoya, for flag and country,” he added.

Eala’s decision to represent her country was backed by lawmakers who called on the government to help pay her $10,000 fine, should it be imposed by the WTA, local news outlets reported.

“If she is being fined because she chose to represent our people, isn’t it only right that the government extends its assistance or support to her?” the Philippine media reported, quoting Senator Erwin Tulfo.

He noted that while the penalty may be a hefty sum of money, it did not compare with the “honour of having one of our best athletes represent our country. I believe it is a price worth paying for.”

The 21-year-old player comes off a career-high season that saw her win her first WTA 1000 title last month and a third-round finish at the US Open. She will compete at the Singapore Open before heading to Japan for the Asian Games, in which she won bronze medals in women’s singles and mixed doubles in Hangzhou, China, in 2022.

Tennis is one of the few sports where a gold medal at the Asian Games doubles as automatic qualification for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics, subject to a top 500 ranking requirement.

articles.title: WTA Finals to move to Charlotte in United States from 2027 on three-year deal
articles.summary: The WTA Finals will take place in the American city of Charlotte from 2027 on a three-year deal.
articles.body:
The American city of Charlotte in North Carolina has been chosen as the new home of the season-ending WTA Finals.

The WTA says it wants to create the "Super Bowl of women's sports" and is hoping the three-year deal will bring more stability to an event that has had six hosts in seven years.

A planned 10-year stay in Shenzhen ended after just one year, with Guadalajara, Fort Worth, Cancun and Riyadh all taking turns since. Crowds have often been disappointing.

"The WTA has always owned the WTA Finals, but now we are going to operate it, too," said WTA chair Valerie Camillo.

"We are not going to do everything ourselves, but we are taking control of this event, of the creation of the revenue and the controlling of the expenses. And that allows us to control our own destiny."

This year's Finals will be held in Indian Wells, California, before the tournament moves to Charlotte from 2027.

Prize money is yet to be announced, but the pot for this year's Finals will be $10m (£7.4m) - which is $5.5m (£4.1m) less than the sum put up by Saudi Arabia last year.

"2026 is a year of transition for the WTA," Camillo said.

"We are doing the normal belt tightening you would expect of any business while also absorbing the unexpected cost of relocating the WTA Finals to Indian Wells.

"What is most important to know is that we have a clear path to deliver consistent, sustainable financial performance in 2027 and beyond, supported by strong revenue and audience growth."

Riyadh had been due to stage the Finals for a third time in November, but the arrangement finished one year early.

This was partly because of the instability caused by the conflict between the United States and Iran, but also reflected the waning interest of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF).

The country's sovereign wealth fund has recently stopped bankrolling LIV Golf, while the Saudi Arabia Snooker Masters was another casualty earlier this year.

The Finals, which involve the best eight singles players and doubles teams of the year, will be staged at the Spectrum Centre where the Charlotte Hornets play their home NBA games.

The basketball season will be in full swing next November and, because of the frequency of home games, the Finals will be reduced from eight days to five, which is likely to affect revenue.

Camillo says the WTA has already started exploring alternative formats with the players, but if the round-robin element of the tournament survives, the finalists would need to play every day.

The WTA will also move its global headquarters from St Petersburg in Florida to Charlotte as part of the agreement.

"We want to create the Super Bowl for women's sports. And not just the competition, but an event that is the annual gathering for women's tennis, women's sports, and women's sport business.

"This is a transformational moment for Charlotte and for our organization," said Will Pitts, CEO of the Charlotte Sports Foundation.

"Bringing the WTA Finals to our city is a testament to what Charlotte has become as a world-class sports destination, and we are incredibly grateful to the WTA for their trust and partnership in making this vision a reality.

articles.body: Las WTA Finals no se mueven de suelo estadounidense. Tras salir Indian Wells como la sede del torneo en 2026, Charlotte (Carolina del Norte) acogerá a las ocho mejores tenistas del año entre 2027 y 2029. La cita tendrá lugar en el Spectrum Center, la casa de los Charlotte Hornets de la NBA. Las finales WTA llevan desde 2014 buscando una sede fija para alojar a sus jugadoras. Singapur fue la más duradera entre 2014 y 2018. Pasó a la ciudad china de Shenzhen en 2019, Guadalajara 2021, Fort Worth (Texas) 2022, Cancún 2023 y las dos últimas ediciones en Riad. Seis localizaciones distintas en los últimos 12 años. Ahora, con Estados Unidos como sede oficial durante las próximas cuatro ediciones, la máxima organización del tenis femenino parece haber encontrado algo de estabilidad. Valerie Camillo, presidente de la WTA, lo describe como un antes y un después: "Las Finales de la WTA representan todo lo que hace que el tenis femenino sea extraordinario. Las mejores atletas del mundo compitiendo al más alto nivel, en un escenario a la altura de sus logros. El tenis femenino ha impulsado el deporte femenino durante generaciones, y ahora tenemos la oportunidad de liderar nuevamente creando una experiencia de campeonato que refleje el gran avance del deporte femenino y hacia dónde se dirige". Y aprovecha para anunciar que Charlotte será la nueva sede mundial de la WTA: "En Charlotte, encontramos más que una ciudad anfitriona. Encontramos socios que comparten esa ambición y un lugar donde podemos construir un verdadero hogar para las Finales y para la WTA”. Will Pitts, director ejecutivo de la Fundación Deportiva de Charlotte, habló desde la perspectiva de la ciudad anfitriona: "Este es un momento trascendental para Charlotte y para nuestra organización. Traer las Finales de la WTA a nuestra ciudad es una muestra de la posición que ha alcanzado Charlotte como destino deportivo de primer nivel, y estamos sumamente agradecidos a la WTA por su confianza y colaboración para hacer realidad esta visión". articles.title: Laver Cup 2026: Schedule, dates, format, players and how to watch or stream Team Europe vs Team World at London's O2 on Sky Sports
articles.summary: Sky Sports will show the Laver Cup live between Friday September 25 and Sunday September 27 as Team Europe face Team World at The O2 in London; Carlos Alcaraz, Alexander Zverev in action; Watch live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, streaming service NOW and the Sky Sports app
articles.body:
Earlier this year, Sky Sports agreed a deal with Trident8 to show all three days of the Laver Cup from London's O2 Arena this month.

Here's everything you need to know about tennis' exciting team event...

The event is played over three days, with four matches on the first two days consisting of three singles contests and one doubles. Six players from Team Europe and six from Team World make up the event.

Matches on Friday are worth one point, Saturday two points and Sunday three points. The winner is the first team to reach 13 points.

If the points are level at 12-12 at the end of all matches, there will be a fifth match on Sunday (The Decider).

All matches are best-of-three sets, which progress to a deciding tiebreak if the opening two sets are shared.

In terms of how the individual matches are decided, a blind draw is used to confirm Friday's clashes.

For Saturday's matches, one team picks from a blind draw first, and the other team then selects their players to face those drawn out.

For Sunday, the reverse then takes place as the other team selects from a blind draw, and the opposing team picks which players they want to play thereafter.

Each player must play in at least one singles contest over the first two days, and no player can play in more than two singles matches.

Like golf's Ryder Cup, the venue alternates between Europe and elsewhere per each edition. It has been held annually since 2017.

The 2026 Laver Cup is being staged at London's O2, while the 2027 event will be hosted at the Intuit Dome in Inglewood, Los Angeles.

Which players are competing in the 2026 Laver Cup?

Frenchman Yannick Noah and the USA's Andre Agassi are the respective captains. Britain's Tim Henman is Team Europe's vice-captain, while Australia's Pat Rafter is Team World's vice-captain.

Team Europe lineup: Spain's Carlos Alcaraz , Germany's Alexander Zverev , Italy's Flavio Cobolli , Spain's Rafael Jodar , Czech Republic's Jakub Mensik and Norway's Casper Ruud.

Team World lineup: USA's Ben Shelton , Australia's Alex de Minaur , USA's Taylor Fritz , USA's Learner Tien , Kazakhstan's Alexander Bublik and Argentina' s Francisco Cerúndolo.

Who are the defending Laver Cup champions?

In 2025, Team World beat Team Europe 15-9 at the Chase Center in San Francisco.

The first day saw Europe 3-1 ahead after singles wins for Ruud over Reilly Opelka and Mensik over Alex Michelsen, and doubles victory for Alcaraz and Mensik over Fritz and Michelsen.

The second day saw domination from Team World, however, as they won all four contests to take a 9-3 lead - De Minaur beating Zverev, Fritz beating Alcaraz, Cerundolo beating Holger Rune and a doubles pairing of De Minaur and Michelsen beating Ruud and Rune.

On the final day, a doubles pairing of Alcaraz and Ruud beat Michelsen and Opelka, and Alcaraz beat Cerundolo in singles, but it wasn't enough as De Minaur beat Mensik and Fritz beat Zverev to wrap up victory.

Henman: Laver Cup a unique opportunity for watching tennis fans

Team Europe vice-captain and Sky Sports Tennis expert Tim Henman said:

"It's a unique opportunity to see the best players in the world coming together to represent Team Europe and Team World at the iconic O2 arena.

"Fans can expect plenty of drama, passion and rivalry, both on and off the court.

"It's great news the Laver Cup will be on Sky Sports."

Hosted by presenter Gigi Salmon, Sky Sports will broadcast all 12 matches across day and night sessions on Friday September 25 and Saturday September 26, followed by a single concluding session on Sunday September 27.

There will also be a reporter on the ground keeping fans abreast of all the news from the weekend's action.

Alongside broadcast rights, fans in the UK and Ireland will also be able to catch up on all the action with clips and highlights available across Sky's digital and social platforms.

articles.body:
Still struggling with injuries, Jack Draper recently ended his 2026 season early.

"Don't usually love lots of words on here, but I wanted to update you that I am aiming to return to the tour at the start of 2027. Last summer, all the dedication and work I had put into this sport was coming together. It was all going my way, and the path seemed so clear. However, a complicated injury made things incredibly challenging, and since that moment I've been desperately trying to get back and feel as I once did on the court," said Draper on Instagram .

"Managing so much change, adversity, and pain has helped me to grow massively in many areas of my life, but has also made me feel a level of fatigue that made it difficult to keep going. I am taking this time to reset and heal, so when I return, I am 100% ready to go.

"Tennis is my purpose and passion, and so when I step back on court, I want to make sure that there's nothing holding me back from where I want to go and achieve the things I know I'm capable of. I really appreciate all the continued support from my sponsors, team, and people who enjoy following my tennis, and I look forward to being back on court to give it my all next year!"

As Draper calls it quits for 2026, what better time than now to look back at every win he picked up this year?

Jack Draper won eight matches this season

The British star established himself as one of the brightest prospects in men's tennis last year. Draper won Indian Wells and reached the Madrid Open final, breaking into the world's top five.

Unfortunately for Draper, a bone bruise in his left arm limited him to one match after Wimbledon, where he won his first-round tie at the US Open before withdrawing. Returning in 2026, Draper began to find form before a separate knee injury forced him out of action. Then, the bone bruise flared up again, bringing his season to a close.

This year didn't go to plan at all, but Draper still managed to win eight matches.

He won his first match of the year in Norway. Competing for Team Great Britain at the Davis Cup, Draper defeated world number 313 Viktor Durasovic in straight sets, 6-2, 6-2. The British star looked impressive on his return, leading many to believe his injury woes were behind him.

However, a late withdrawal from the Rotterdam Open brought those questions back to the fore. Draper instead returned to ATP Tour action in the UAE at the Dubai Tennis Championships. There, Draper beat the Frenchman Quentin Halys, 7-6, 6-3, to reach the second round. He fell short against another Frenchman, Arthur Rinderknech, in round two, but looked strong in defeat.

His next task was to defend the Indian Wells title he won in 2025. Draper found himself in trouble early on, losing the opening set of his second-round match, but recovered to beat Roberto Bautista Agut, 3-6, 6-3, 6-2. Then, in the third round, Draper defeated top-20 star Francisco Cerundolo to set up a blockbuster last-16 clash with Novak Djokovic. Picking up the biggest win of his 2026 campaign, Draper beat Djokovic , 4-6, 6-4, 7-5. Daniil Medvedev then ended Draper's title defence in the quarter-finals, winning 6-1, 7-5.

In Miami, Draper lost his opening match to Reilly Opelka before retiring due to injury against Tomas Martin Etcheverry in Barcelona. He didn't play another match on clay and returned on grass, looking to snap a three-match losing streak.

He did just that, beating Marcos Giron in the first round of the Eastbourne Open and his countryman, Jack Pinnington Jones, in the second round. Draper then defeated Gabriel Diallo 6-1, 6-4 to reach his first ATP semi-final of the season. He fell short in his bid to reach the final, though, losing to Ugo Humbert in straights.

Draper didn't win another match post-Eastbourne. He lost his opening matches in Canada and Cincinnati before he ended his season early.

Where will Jack Draper be ranked by the end of 2026?

Draper finished 2022, 2023, 2024, and 2025 as a top-100 player. However, that streak will end in 2026. Draper currently sits 151st in the 'Live ATP Rankings', but risks falling further out of contention.

He is 136th in the 'Live ATP Race', and without playing any more matches this year, Draper will continue to see players pass him over the coming months.

articles.title: Novak Djokovic to return to ATP's China Open on Sky Sports after 11-year absence from event
articles.summary: Novak Djokovic announces he will return to ATP Tour's China Open for first time since 2015 between September 30-October 6, live on Sky Sports; Decision comes following shock US Open first-round exit; watch Laver Cup at O2 in London from 25-27 September live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
The 39-year-old recently dropped as low as No 12 in the world rankings following a shock first-round defeat to Argentina's Mariano Navone at the US Open.

That defeat followed on from a third-round exit in May at the French Open - two underwhelming Grand Slam displays coming either side of a run to the semi-finals at Wimbledon, where he was well beaten in straight sets by eventual champion Jannik Sinner.

Djokovic has not won a Grand Slam title since 2023, going three full calendar years without success.

Returning to the ‌ATP 500 event in Beijing, Djokovic is a six-time winner having last competed there in 2015. Sinner won the title last year, but is currently out with a knee injury.

Defeat to Navone in New York marked the first time Djokovic had lost an opening round contest at a Grand Slam since the 2006 Australian Open.

"I am excited to come back and perform in front of all of you at the National Tennis Centre - one of the nicest venues we have in tennis," Djokovic said on an Instagram story on Wednesday.

Also on Wednesday, news came that Britain's Emma Raducanu has withdrawn from this month's China Open and will not return to action until October at the earliest.

Raducanu has not played since losing the Queen's Club final in June, missing Wimbledon and the US Open due to a stress fracture in her leg.

The 23-year-old has returned to training after she shared video footage last week of herself in London's National Tennis Centre.

Raducanu could return at the Wuhan Open on October 12, live on Sky Sports .

Stream tennis with no contract on NOW and the Sky Sports App . You can also watch the Laver Cup at The O2 in London from 25-27 September live on Sky Sports.

articles.title: Guadalajara Open: Marta Kostyuk through to quarter-finals without playing a point
articles.summary: Marta Kostyuk is through to the quarter-finals of the Guadalajara Open even though the top seed is yet to play a point in the tournament.
articles.body:
Marta Kostyuk is through to the quarter-finals of the Guadalajara Open even though the top seed is yet to play a point in the tournament.

The Ukrainian received a first-round bye in Mexico and got a walkover in her scheduled second-round match on Wednesday, when Taylor Townsend withdrew because of an illness.

Kostyuk, the world number 10, is now scheduled to get her tournament under way against the eighth-seeded Liudmila Samsonova of Russia, who edged Kayla Day 7-6 (7-4) 2-6 7-6 (7-5).

Kostyuk claimed her maiden WTA 1000 title in Madrid in May and has reached the semi-finals of the French Open and Wimbledon this year.

Most recently the 24-year-old lost to sixth seed Linda Noskova in the last 16 of the US Open.

articles.title: 'I'm done playing the victim': Sumit Nagal reveals 'change' in mindset after difficult 2026
articles.summary: Tennis News: India’s top-ranked singles player Sumit Nagal has had a difficult 2026 season, with injuries disrupting his progress and pushing him down to No. 247 i.
articles.body: India’s top-ranked singles player Sumit Nagal has had a difficult 2026 season, with injuries disrupting his progress and pushing him down to No. 247 in the rankings. But the 29-year-old says he has changed his mindset and is now focused more on enjoying tennis than constantly worrying about results.Nagal started the year with a hip injury picked up during a Challenger event in Thailand. He returned early for India’s Davis Cup tie against the Netherlands in Bengaluru because he wanted to represent the country."I started the year with an injury, then played Davis Cup (in Bengaluru). I was always running behind time. I came in early to play because it was Davis Cup and Team India," Nagal told PTI."If it wasn't for the Davis Cup, I would have taken the whole month off.”He later developed a wrist problem and said he did not feel fully fit until May."I was in a position where I wasn't healthy, but I was playing. And then March, again, I started feeling something in my wrist. So I didn't feel good till I would say May."Nagal changes his approachDespite the setbacks, Nagal won a Challenger title in Romania and reached another semifinal in Czechia. He believes his game has improved in recent months.“The last two, three months have been better comparing to the first half of the year. And now I just have to build on it," he said.His US Open qualifying campaign ended with a 3-6, 6-7(4) loss to France’s Arthur Gea. Nagal, however, felt the close match showed he can still compete at a high level."My last match in the US Open was a little bit unfortunate. I had a few break points and the guy ended up making the fourth round. So I feel like it's there, it's just I need to work hard for it to go in my favour," he said.The constant cycle of playing and recovering also affected him mentally."It's not so fun, because when you play for two months and then you're out for two months and you play for two months, I don't think it's so much fun. But I'm done playing the victim. I take it as what it is, how it is, and I try to enjoy every day.Before the US Open, Nagal realised he needed to stop putting all his focus on winning."I realised that I need to be more happy. Very simple, actually. And not focus too much about winning, winning, winning, winning. Because I was doing that and it wasn't really working for me."A loss to Jan Kumsat in Prague helped him reach that realisation."I lost a match in Prague and I was driving back. And that's when I realised, I said, man, like this is just not fun. I'm not going to survive like this if I keep putting pressure on myself that every match I step on, I need to win, win, win,” Nagal said."I was just burning too much energy throughout the match and throughout the days."'The focus right now is to compete’Nagal has also put his immediate goal of returning to the top 100 aside."You always want to play the Slams. You want to be top 50, top 30. But I wouldn't say that's my focus right now. The focus right now is to compete, man," he said.Earlier in the season, he often struggled to maintain his level throughout matches."For a lot of weeks, I was playing two good sets and not the third set. That's very basic. Or I was playing one good set and not a good second set because I was just playing the victim thing and saying, ‘Oh, this is not working for myself. This is not working. This is against me. Everything was against me’," he said.“And like this, whatever, you can have any goals. But like this, you're not going to reach anywhere.”Nagal is also willing to help younger Indian players but does not want to force himself into a leadership role.“I'm always open for them. I guide them if something is needed. But also, I don't want to be in there, let's say, as a leadership role when it's not asked,” he said.“At the end of the day, it's still a team sport. It shouldn't be one guy leading the team. Of course, my help is there. I've always said it. I always want Indian tennis to do well. Never a question.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
